clue.text: Conservatively-run hostelry is said to be making changes

indicators.note: is said tells us the phrase for a Tory's pub is spoken, not spelt, to give the entry

parts.note: a hostelry run by a Conservative is an inn of a Tory, inn-o'-a-Tory when said quickly

explanation.surface: A pub run on Tory lines is rumoured to be shaking things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservatively-run' suggests a cautious manager, but it means owned by a Tory (a member of Britain's Conservative Party): 'inn of a Tory', run together in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovatory person or idea brings in new methods, so it is busy making changes.

clue.text: One gets a doctor to see this foot

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone sees a doctor about their foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the poetic sense: a unit of metre.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical unit of one unstressed syllable then one stressed, a foot in verse.

clue.text: Bare rocky dune

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of dune wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A stony sand hill with nothing growing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude means naked, uncovered, a synonym of bare.

clue.text: Six get free petrol in Paris sound to be going green

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to rid is to free

indicators.note: sound tells us the French word for petrol is spoken, and its sound gives the closing letters

parts.note: essence is the French word for petrol

explanation.surface: Six people get free fuel in France, and the noise makes them turn green.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash before 'sound', which here means 'sounding like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Viridescence is the quality of becoming green, from the Latin viridis.

clue.text: Disapproval it's given rise to for everybody

parts.note: tut is the sound of disapproval

indicators.note: given rise, in a down clue, means the word it is read upward, that is backwards

parts.note: the word it, with the 's (has) serving only as a link

explanation.surface: Someone's disapproval has caused the whole crowd to react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given rise' reverses IT to TI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all performers together, Italian for all.

clue.text: Space for jumper on the road to the Cape

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
M1 is the main motorway out of London, so the road gives MI
a ness is a cape or headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: Room is needed for a kangaroo travelling the highway towards the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jumper' in Britain is also a sweater, but here it is the leaper. M1 (London to Yorkshire motorway) is written MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Roominess is spaciousness, the amount of room available.

clue.text: Note to man returning to the country

indicators.note: returning sends the note and the man back the way they came, so both are read right to left

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
Al is a man's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A message is sent to a man coming home to his native land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole run SO + AL, giving LAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in South-East Asia, so it is a country.

clue.text: About one, the Queen has a port

indicators.note: About means the queen's name goes around the letter for one

parts.note: Alexandra was Queen consort of Edward VII
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Around one o'clock, Her Majesty has a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is a harbour city. Queen Alexandra was the wife of King Edward VII.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is a major Egyptian harbour city on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Potholing most of the time; not starting the study of rocks

indicators.note: most of means the word for time loses its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: not starting means the study of rocks loses its first letter

parts.note: geology is the science of rocks

explanation.surface: Cave exploring takes up nearly all of someone's time; they are not taking up rock science.
explanation.definitionFit: Speleology is the scientific study and exploration of caves, popularly known as caving.

clue.text: 26 has its share of sweet reasonableness

parts.note: 26 refers to the answer of 26 across, which is mode
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone, or something numbered 26, is getting its fair portion of good nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 is a cross-reference: put in the answer to 26 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation is the quality of avoiding extremes, a calm, reasonable temper.

clue.text: Announced end of holiday

indicators.note: Announced means the word for end is spoken aloud, and its sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: fate is one's end or doom

explanation.surface: The close of the vacation has been made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of holiday' looks like the last letter of a word, but 'end' is FATE spoken, and 'holiday' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or festive day, a sort of public holiday celebration.

clue.text: What those in service do, according to Milton

definitions.text: What those in service do, according to Milton

parts.words: What those in service do, according to Milton
parts.note: Milton's sonnet on his blindness ends 'They also serve who only' remain still and attend, which is what servants do

explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests domestic servants, but Milton's line is about serving God by patient waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton wrote that those who stay still and attend also serve, the closing line of his sonnet on blindness.

clue.text: Manage to get tired, stamina failing

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters of tired and stamina breaking down and being rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone who has run out of energy is finding it a struggle to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' signals the anagram of TIRED and STAMINA, which together make the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to run or direct affairs, a synonym of manage.

clue.text: Mental aberration finds support in "The Tempest"

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
a tempest is a storm

explanation.surface: A mental lapse is found to underpin Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tempest' looks like the Shakespeare title; read it as a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a brainstorm is a sudden mental lapse or fit of confusion.

clue.text: Occupation of sprightly outlaw, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us a lively outlaw's name is spoken, and that sound is what is written

parts.note: sprightly means lively, and Robin Hood is the outlaw, so lively Hood

explanation.surface: The trade of an energetic bandit, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A livelihood is the job or means by which someone earns a living.

clue.text: Put back to control the body politic

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse's reins
the body politic is the state, the people organised under a government

explanation.surface: Someone is restored to office to run the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position, which is to put them back.

clue.text: Outline of a silly tax

parts.note: dumb means silly or stupid
a rate is a tax, as in local rates

explanation.surface: A sketch of a foolish levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outline' is a verb here; British 'rates' were a local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or give a faint preliminary indication of something.

clue.text: Like a swelling boy has on back

indicators.note: back sends the boy and the word on in the reverse direction, read right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster with a lump on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run LAD + ON, giving NO + DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or swelling in the body, and nodal is its adjective.

clue.text: Single Frenchman marries the girl

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: An unmarried man from France weds the young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marries' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name, so it fits the girl in the clue.

clue.text: Cowboy tune one sang getting out of the saddle

indicators.note: cowboy used as an adjective means slapdash, so the letters of tune, one and sang are botched into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cowboy song somebody sang while dismounting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy' as in a cowboy builder means badly done, signalling the anagram of TUNE, I and SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseating a rider throws them off, so they come out of the saddle.

clue.text: Change of directors' in control centres

parts.note: to switch is to change
a company's directors sit on its board, so boards stands for directors

explanation.surface: A reshuffle of the board of directors in the company's headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard is the panel where telephone lines or circuits are connected and managed.

clue.text: A politician has one defence

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A politician has a single line of defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that one was elsewhere, a defence against a charge.

clue.text: Stream with char in in it

definitions.meaning: in Scotland a small stream is called a ...
to char is to scorch or blacken by fire

explanation.walkthrough: The char is also a fish found in highland streams; 'in in it' plays on the stream having char in it, and char meaning to burn in.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a brook, and a verb for scorching with fire.

clue.text: Just the girl, say, for this man

indicators.note: say tells us the girl's name is spoken and the man's name sounds the same

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman would be perfect for this fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene is a man's name, short for Eugene.

clue.text: Band leader wearing spectacles has note for player

indicators.note: wearing puts the band's first letter inside the spectacles, as eyes wear glasses

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of round spectacles

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word Band

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A bespectacled bandleader carries a message for one of the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts B (the first letter of 'Band') inside OO, the picture of spectacles; then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, and the name also stands for the person who plays it in an orchestra.

clue.text: Ludicrous imitation makes curia react badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of curia and react are reacting in a disordered way and rearranged

explanation.surface: The papal court overreacts, producing a farcical parody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals the anagram of CURIA and REACT; the curia is the Pope's court.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is a grotesquely exaggerated portrait, a mocking copy of its subject.

clue.text: Fashion mannequin left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is dropped from the word for mannequin

parts.note: a model is a mannequin, either a dummy or a person showing clothes

explanation.surface: A fashion model has been omitted from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a style or vogue, which is what fashion means here.

clue.text: 'Omes, say, for the maquis

definitions.meaning: 'omes is the Cockney way of saying ohms, the units in which electrical opposition to current is measured
the maquis were the French guerrillas fighting the German occupation in the Second World War

explanation.walkthrough: 'Omes is how a Cockney (who drops his h) says 'homes', but it sounds like ohms, the units of electrical opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohms measure electrical opposition to current, and the maquis formed the underground movement against German occupation of France.
